title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge. Jianyu Wei, Shijie Cao, Ting Cao, Lingxiao Ma, Lei Wang, Yanyong Zhang, Mao Yang (USTC/UCAS/Microsoft Research). EuroSys '25 (Rotterdam, Mar 30-Apr 3 2025), doi 10.1145/3689031.3696099
id_read: arXiv 2407.00088v2 (25 Mar 2025), full PDF via pdftotext (15 pp)
setup: Llama-2-7B/13B at 1/2/3/4 bit (4-bit = GPTQ Q4_0-style gguf; 2/3-bit from BitDistiller QAT; 1-bit from OneBit) and BitNet-b1.58-3B. Devices (Table 2): Apple M2-Ultra 16 cores 819.2 GB/s; Raspberry Pi 5 4xA76 17.1 GB/s; Jetson AGX Orin 12xA78AE 204.8 GB/s; Surface Book 3 i5-1035G7 4 cores 58.2 GB/s (the only x86 box). Later Table 6/7: Surface Laptop 7 (Snapdragon X Elite, 4 of 12 cores), OnePlus 12, Jetson Orin NX. Baseline llama.cpp b2794 (May 2024) dequantise kernels (and BLAS for GEMM). Batch 1 for GEMV/decode; mpGEMM test uses seq 256. E2E: 64 tokens x 20 iterations. Method: weights split into 1-bit planes, activation groups of g=4 precomputed into 16-entry tables held in one register (ARM TBL / AVX2 PSHUF), int8 table quantisation, optional fast 8-bit aggregation (FA).

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: average 3.6x over llama.cpp dequant kernels 'at 1-2 bit'
catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: 3.6x average is stated for all kernels/devices vs llama.cpp (Sec 1); the paper does not restrict it to 1-2 bit. Per-bit maxima are 11.2/5.8/4.7/3.1x
2.8x is in the intro for the 2-bit model, but Fig 8's order gives 2.8x to the 4-bit model on RPi5 single thread and 6.7x to 2-bit; internally inconsistent. Multi-thread M2-Ultra e2e is only 1.1-2.3x
5.65 -> 7.34 (1.30x), same PPL as llama.cpp

catalog_numbers_correct.claim: first-pass: Table 7 Surface Laptop 7 21.63 vs 10.64 at 4 bit

catalog_numbers_correct.true_value: llama.cpp b2794, May 2024; T-MAC's own text says llama.cpp gains nothing below 4 bit and 3-bit is 15% slower than 4-bit

why: Assumptions that break: (1) baseline is a 2024 dequantise+FMA kernel at 1-3 bit, while our baseline is a tuned int8 dot on Q4-class weights; the only 4-bit comparison on a like-for-like weight file (Table 4, same Q4_0 model) gives 1.30x single-thread and the paper says multi-thread is bandwidth-limited. (2) T-MAC tables are bit-serial (activation groups of 4 against 1-bit weight planes, pshufb/tbl in-register), not 8-dim VQ codebook gathers, so it does not test our gather LUT (our own gather kernel 0.06-0.17x of int8 dot is not contradicted). (3) Only one x86 device (4-core i5-1035G7, 58 GB/s), no AVX2 number is broken out. (4) Weights are in RAM; no NVMe streaming; in our regime at 8 GB the expert stream is the bottleneck, so a compute-kernel gain only matters at 16/32 GB hit rates. (5) 2/3-bit models need QAT (BitDistiller/OneBit); 4-bit needs nothing.
quality_loss: None for the table-lookup itself at 4-bit (identical PPL 5.96 to llama.cpp Q4_0, Table 4); Table 3 NMSE 3.35e-3 vs 3.33e-3 llama.cpp for 4096x4096. Fast aggregation: +0.42 wiki PPL, +1.04 lambada PPL, WinoGrande 70.8 -> 67.8. Low-bit models' own quality (2-bit via BitDistiller) is not evaluated by this paper.
ablation: Yes (Sec 5.5, Fig 10): TM-base up to 17% slower than llama.cpp; table quantisation brings parity; tiling up to 1.45x; permutation 1.39x; tuning small. Isolates kernel design only; no cache/layout/prefetch notion.
limitations: Authors say multi-thread mpGEMV is constrained by memory bandwidth and e2e gains shrink due to non-GEMV operators; FA hurts quality; M2-Ultra GEMM loses to AMX BLAS (T-MAC max 2.0x at 1-bit). No dedicated limitations section.
contradicts_our_findings: No. It supports our 'bytes half only' reading: gains vanish when memory-bound (multi-thread e2e 1.1-2.3x on M2-Ultra; 4-bit Table 4 only 1.3x). Our gather-LUT result (0.06-0.17x of int8 dot) is for a different table design and is neither confirmed nor refuted. Paper-internal inconsistency (2.8x) noted above.

why: (1) Baseline FP32: 16x more bytes than the 2-bit codes yet only 2.75-4x faster, so against a Q4 int8 kernel that already runs at memory speed the ratio is <=1 (the AQLM kernel is not bandwidth-bound; derived 17 GB/s of codes). (2) Needs expensive post-training with fine-tuning (days of A100) that we cannot do for a 125B MoE. (3) Codebooks are per-matrix learned, not shared across 512 experts; Mixtral was only done at 1x16 with GPU kernels. (4) At 2 bit quality loss is material (7B -5 pt avg acc). (5) Weights in RAM; no NVMe. The byte reduction (2.0 vs 4.3 bpw) is the part that could transfer and equals what IQ2 already ships.
quality_loss: See numbers: 7B 2x8 +1.45 PPL after fine-tune (+2.49 before); 2-bit Mixtral -4.65 pt avg acc, Wiki2 3.46 -> 4.61. MMLU/GSM8k relative degradation 'higher than on standard evals' (App. K).
ablation: Yes: fine-tuning scope (Table 7), codebook count/group (Table 9: 2x8gs8 7.61, 4x8gs16 8.14, 8x8gs32 7.38, 15x8gs64 7.85 untuned), calibration size (Table 8). No cache/layout notion.
limitations: Authors: more expensive to quantise than RTN/GPTQ; smaller 8-bit codebooks (needed for fast CPU/GPU kernels) raise quantisation error; better fine-tuning left for future work.
contradicts_our_findings: No. Consistent with our reading that published LUT-kernel gains are vs FP32/FP16. Additionally shows the AQLM CPU kernel is lookup/compute-bound (6x lower byte rate than baseline), the same direction as our gather-LUT result. Note the AQLM kernel itself was not run by us.

title: KBVQ-MoE: KLT-Guided SVD with Bias-Corrected Vector Quantization for MoE Large Language Models. Zukang Xu, Zhixiong Zhao, Xing Hu, Zhixuan Chen, Dawei Yang (Houmo AI; Nanyang Technological University). 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'
id_read: arXiv 2602.11184v2 (24 Feb 2026; v1 submitted 30 Jan 2026), full PDF via pdftotext. First pass read v1 via digest and could not confirm the venue; v2 header confirms ICLR 2026
setup: Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (14.3B total, 60 experts, from memory), Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts, top-8), Mixtral-8x7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Method: KLT-guided SVD pulls shared low-rank part across experts (rank = 1/128 of full; about 0.08 extra bits per weight, 2.08 effective bits for the 2-bit setting), VQ with vector length 4 (not 8) on the residual per expert (k-means++, 100 iters), channel-wise affine bias correction. title: A Multi-Engine Dataflow for MoE Decoding on AWS Tranium [sic, in the title; Trainium in the text] (CARDAN). Bin Ma (UC Merced), Wenjie Fan (Yotta Labs), Jonny Liu (Yotta Labs), Dong Li (UC Merced / Yotta Labs)
id_read: arXiv 2609.21137v4 (20 Oct 2026; v1 17 Sep 2026), full PDF via pdftotext -layout and raw mode. First pass could only read the abstract
setup: AWS Trainium3 (8 NeuronCore-v4, 144 GiB HBM at 4.7 TB/s, 64 MiB SBUF per logical core), TP=4, batch-1 TPOT. Models (Table 2): Qwen3-30B-A3B (48 layers, 128 experts, top-8), DeepSeek-V2-Lite (64, top-6), Nemotron-3-Nano-30B (128, top-6), OLMoE-1B-7B (64, top-8), Gemma-4-26B-A4B (128, top-8). Baselines: PyTorch/XLA and AWS BF16 dense MoE megakernel (production AWS/NxDI for Qwen3 and Gemma, ported design for the others). Representation: gate and up matrices only = per-layer shared VQ codebook (K=256, uint8 index maps per expert, block d=8 or 4, looked up by GpSimd 'indexed selection') + shared-basis low-rank (rank r, per-expert coefficients); down projection stays BF16. why: Accelerator with software-managed scratchpad and DMA engines (the bottleneck is HBM DMA at 4.7 TB/s, not NVMe at ~3-7 GB/s, i.e. ~1000x different), tensor-parallel 4-way, BF16 weights, 30B-class models with 64-128 experts, training/distillation required, gate/up only. The result that does transfer: lookups are not free. When the block size shrinks to d=2 to keep quality, the extra indexed selections (GpSimd) made decode slower than the dense BF16 baseline despite 12% fewer bytes. That is the same trade our gather-LUT microbenchmark found on CPU.
quality_loss: With distillation PPL is at or below the BF16 teacher on all five (-1.1% to -4.9%); without training (closed form) +27% PPL on Qwen3, +49% DS-V2-Lite; VQ-only d=8 collapses (PPL 451). Downstream: Qwen3 loses up to 3.2 pt on four zero-shot tasks.
ablation: Yes, the most useful of the batch: representation (VQ-only vs LR-only vs hybrid, Table 6), kernel mechanisms (Table 4A), fusion (4B), d=2 equal-rate lookup cost (Table 3, Sec 5.5), batch scaling. No cache or prefetch ablation (it argues prefetch is awkward on a scratchpad).
limitations: No dedicated limitations section found; boundary conditions stated in Sec 5.5 (d=2 is slower, K fixed at 256 for uint8 index, only gate/up compressed). Related: MoBE (arXiv 2508.05257) for the shared basis, cited as ref [5].
contradicts_our_findings: No. Independent support for our refutation of the compute half (lookup work cancels byte savings once blocks are small), and the closest published combination of our families 2 and 5 (shared codebook + shared low-rank basis across experts) - but gains are 1.15-1.31x at batch 1 on an HBM accelerator.
